607	<main id="content">
608	<article>
609	<section class="hero" id="top"><div class="wrap"><div class="hero-copy"><h1 class="heading-1 heading-gradient"><span class="keep">Two-way</span><span class="br mob"></span> sync<span class="br desk"></span> of<span class="br mob"></span> customer<span class="br mob"></span> and<span class="br desk"></span> contact<span class="br mob"></span> records</h1><p class="body-3 measure">Tequity builds software for clients. This is the Round 1 exercise.</p><p class="body-3 measure">Plan on about 4 hours. Most of that time is the design.</p><p class="body-3 measure">Send the deliverables on the calendar thread within 24 hours of receiving this assignment, or before your interview call, whichever is earlier.</p><p class="body-3 measure">The next round will be scheduled based on your performance.</p><p class="body-3 measure">Where this note is silent, write the assumption and the question you would have asked. We will read that list.</p></div></div></section>
610	<section class="section reveal" id="background-and-scenario"><div class="wrap"><header class="section-head"><div class="kicker"><i class="ph ph-buildings" aria-hidden="true"></i></div><h2 class="heading-2">Background and scenario</h2></header><div class="section-body"><p class="body-3 measure">A client runs its sales team in Salesforce, a customer relationship management (CRM) product. Tequity has built the client an operations portal. Finance and customer-success staff work in the portal.</p><p class="body-3 measure">The same people exist in both places, as customers and as contacts. A sales person creates a customer in Salesforce. The portal should show that customer. A finance person on the portal then corrects the billing city. Salesforce should show the new city. Later, a sales person changes the phone number in Salesforce. The portal should show the new phone, and the city the finance person set should still be there.</p><p class="body-3 measure">The client also needs the history. They need to know who changed the phone, and who changed the city. The fact of an earlier edit stays on record after a later edit.</p><p class="body-3 measure">Salesforce stores its own copy. The portal stores its copy in PostgreSQL (Postgres). The two copies have to stay in sync. We are designing and building our side. Salesforce already exists, and it stays as it is.</p></div></div></section>
611	<section class="section reveal" id="the-systems-involved"><div class="wrap"><header class="section-head"><div class="kicker"><i class="ph ph-share-network" aria-hidden="true"></i></div><h2 class="heading-2">The systems involved</h2></header><div class="section-body"><p class="body-3 measure">Three parties matter.</p><ol class="cards cols-3 wide"><li><div class="body-3"><strong>Salesforce.</strong> The client's CRM. Sales users edit records here. Salesforce has its own database.</div></li><li><div class="body-3"><strong>The portal.</strong> Our application. Finance and customer-success users edit records here. Our database is Postgres.</div></li><li><div class="body-3"><strong>The network between them.</strong> Salesforce and the portal talk over the public internet, using Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure (HTTPS). Each side keeps its own database. HTTPS is the only path between them.</div></li></ol><p class="title-3 measure">Who calls whom:</p><ul class="list list-ul measure"><li><div>When a record changes in Salesforce, Salesforce calls us. The call is a webhook: an HTTPS request to an endpoint we host. The webhook names the record and describes the change.</div></li><li><div>When a record changes in the portal, we call Salesforce. The call uses Salesforce's official record application programming interface (API): the create and update operations Salesforce already documents. The portal reaches Salesforce through that record API.</div></li><li><div>A sales user talks only to Salesforce. A portal user talks only to the portal. Neither user talks to the other system.</div></li></ul><p class="body-3 measure">The rate limit below applies to the requests we send to Salesforce. Webhooks Salesforce sends to us sit outside that cap.</p><div class="frame frame-diagram measure"><pre><code> Sales user                         Finance / customer-success user
612	     |                                          |
613	     | uses                                     | uses
614	     v                                          v
615	 Salesforce CRM                           Tequity portal
616	 (their app, their database)              (our app)
617	     |                                          |
618	     |                                          v
619	     |                                     Postgres
620	     |                                     (our database)
621	     |
622	     |   (A) Salesforce calls us
623	     |       HTTPS webhook
624	     +----------------------------------&gt;  portal webhook endpoint
625	     |
626	     |   (B) We call Salesforce
627	     |       HTTPS record API
628	     &lt;----------------------------------+  portal sync worker
629	           create or update record</code></pre></div><p class="body-3 measure">The webhook endpoint and the sync worker are both ours. They can be one service or two. Say which you choose, and what crosses the boundary between them.</p><p class="body-3 measure">A webhook is a message. Our endpoint has to accept it, check it, and apply it before anything is stored. A call to the Salesforce record API is a request we initiate. Salesforce may accept it, reject it, or be unreachable.</p></div></div></section>
630	<section class="section reveal" id="requirements-and-scale"><div class="wrap"><header class="section-head"><div class="kicker"><i class="ph ph-list-checks" aria-hidden="true"></i></div><h2 class="heading-2">Requirements and scale</h2></header><div class="section-body"><p class="title-3 measure">Records:</p><ul class="list list-ul measure"><li><div>Customers and contacts. About these fields, and no others, for this exercise: customer name, status, and owner; contact full name, phone, email, city, owner, and the customer they belong to.</div></li><li><div><strong>5 million records</strong> in production, customers and contacts counted together.</div></li></ul><p class="title-3 measure">Sync:</p><ul class="list list-ul measure"><li><div>While both systems are up, a create or an update on either side is visible on the other side within <strong>30 seconds</strong>. Thirty seconds is the worst case. Everyday sync should land sooner.</div></li><li><div>Both sides may create. Both sides may update.</div></li><li><div>The current value of a field is the one we can justify. The earlier values, who made them, and when, stay on record. Dropping that history counts as losing a change.</div></li><li><div>An update we send to Salesforce must not bounce back and forth forever.</div></li></ul><p class="title-3 measure">Webhooks:</p><ul class="list list-ul measure"><li><div>Salesforce may deliver the same webhook twice.</div></li><li><div>Salesforce may deliver webhooks in a different order from the order of the edits.</div></li><li><div>Each webhook carries at least the fields in the sample below. <code>occurredAt</code> is the time Salesforce gives the event.</div></li></ul><p class="body-3 measure">The CRM API allows at most <strong>100 requests per second</strong>. That is our cap on calls to Salesforce. We choose how far under the cap to run.</p><p class="body-3 measure">We left the peak edit rate open. State the rate you assume, in edits per second, and use it in the arithmetic.</p><p class="body-3 measure">Sample webhook. This is enough to start. You may add fields. Say why.</p><div class="frame frame-json measure"><pre><code>{
631	  &quot;eventId&quot;: &quot;evt_1001&quot;,
632	  &quot;recordId&quot;: &quot;0031A00000Abc&quot;,
633	  &quot;objectType&quot;: &quot;Contact&quot;,
634	  &quot;occurredAt&quot;: &quot;2026-11-02T11:30:04.000Z&quot;,
635	  &quot;changedBy&quot;: &quot;sales.user@client.example&quot;,
636	  &quot;changedFields&quot;: {
637	    &quot;phone&quot;: &quot;+919876543210&quot;
638	  }
639	}</code></pre></div><p class="body-3 measure">Sample portal edit. A finance user saved the form. The sample has no time field. Decide where the time and the actor come from, and write that down.</p><div class="frame frame-json measure"><pre><code>{
640	  &quot;recordId&quot;: &quot;0031A00000Abc&quot;,
641	  &quot;objectType&quot;: &quot;Contact&quot;,
642	  &quot;editedBy&quot;: &quot;finance.user@client.example&quot;,
643	  &quot;changedFields&quot;: {
644	    &quot;city&quot;: &quot;Noida&quot;
645	  }
646	}</code></pre></div><p class="body-3 measure">Say whether you assume a webhook carries only the changed fields, or the full record. Pick one in the design. Say what your rule does in the other case.</p></div></div></section>
647	<section class="section reveal" id="constraints"><div class="wrap"><header class="section-head"><div class="kicker"><i class="ph ph-barricade" aria-hidden="true"></i></div><h2 class="heading-2">Constraints</h2></header><div class="section-body"><p class="body-3 measure"><strong>Rate limit.</strong> At most 100 requests per second to the Salesforce record API. The cap counts the calls we make, including retries. Webhooks arriving at our endpoint sit outside this cap. If Salesforce tells us to slow down, we slow down, and we keep the work.</p><p class="body-3 measure"><strong>Outages.</strong> Design for the Salesforce API being unreachable for <strong>6 hours</strong>. Webhooks Salesforce tried to send during that window may never arrive. Pending calls to Salesforce must still be there after our own process restarts.</p><p class="body-3 measure">Thirty seconds applies while both systems are up. Catch-up after an outage is a different target. Drain the backlog as fast as the rate limit allows. Compute how long that takes, in minutes, for the edit rate you assumed. Show the division.</p><p class="body-3 measure"><strong>Consistency.</strong> Two people may edit the same record at the same time, on the same side or on opposite sides. Edits to different fields of that record both have to survive. Edits to the same field need one current value and a kept history.</p><p class="body-3 measure">Say what you use to decide which edit is current, on a webhook and on a portal save. Name the field. If you need an API this note does not give you, mark it as an assumption.</p><p class="body-3 measure"><strong>Out of scope for this weekend:</strong> deletes, Salesforce login screens, a visual user interface, a second region, and a load test against real Salesforce. If you write a program, call a fake CRM you write yourself.</p></div></div></section>
648	<section class="section reveal" id="what-you-deliver"><div class="wrap"><header class="section-head"><div class="kicker"><i class="ph ph-files" aria-hidden="true"></i></div><h2 class="heading-2">What you deliver</h2></header><div class="section-body"><p class="body-3 measure">Three things are required. A program is optional.</p><p class="tagline heading-3" data-tagline><span class="word">We</span> <span class="word">ask</span> <span class="word">for</span> <span class="word">the</span> <span class="word">chats</span> <span class="word">and</span> <span class="word">the</span> <span class="word">commits</span> <span class="word">because</span> <span class="word">we</span> <span class="word">want</span> <span class="word">to</span> <span class="word">see</span> <span class="word">how</span> <span class="word">you</span> <span class="word">prompt</span> <span class="word">the</span> <span class="word">artificial</span> <span class="word">intelligence</span> <span class="word">(AI)</span> <span class="word">assistant,</span> <span class="word">and</span> <span class="word">how</span> <span class="word">your</span> <span class="word">thinking</span> <span class="word">develops.</span> <span class="word">The</span> <span class="word">final</span> <span class="word">document</span> <span class="word">alone</span> <span class="word">does</span> <span class="word">not</span> <span class="word">show</span> <span class="word">that.</span></p><div class="panel measure"><div class="panel-body"><h3 class="heading-4">1. The design document</h3><p class="body-3 measure">This is the main piece, a few pages, long enough for the rules and the arithmetic. Write it so a teammate who was not on the call can build from it.</p><p class="body-3 measure">These four have to be in it, with a rule for each:</p><ul class="list list-ul measure"><li><div>a duplicate webhook</div></li><li><div>a change that arrives out of order</div></li><li><div>a sync loop, where our own update comes back</div></li><li><div>the 6-hour Salesforce outage, including the minutes of arithmetic</div></li></ul><p class="title-3 measure">Use this outline:</p><ol class="list list-ol measure"><li><div>Assumptions, and the questions you would ask before you lock the design.</div></li><li><div>The systems, who calls whom, the network boundary, and the interface on each side.</div></li><li><div>The subproblems, in the order you would build them. Name the subproblems first. Add a component only when a subproblem needs it.</div></li><li><div>The data you store.</div></li><li><div>The inbound path, from webhook to our database.</div></li><li><div>The outbound path, from a portal edit to a Salesforce API call.</div></li><li><div>The rule when both sides change the same record.</div></li><li><div>The rule for a duplicate webhook, and for an older webhook that arrives after a newer one.</div></li><li><div>The rule that stops a loop.</div></li><li><div>The 6-hour outage: what is on disk, how you drain it, and the minutes of arithmetic.</div></li><li><div>Three numbers you would watch, and the value at which you would call someone.</div></li><li><div>What you are leaving out of this weekend's work.</div></li></ol></div></div><div class="panel measure"><div class="panel-body"><h3 class="heading-4">2. Your full AI chat history, unedited</h3><p class="body-3 measure">Include every chat you used for this task, every prompt, and every reply.</p><p class="body-3 measure">Do not clean the chats up, trim them, or rewrite them. Leave the wrong turns in. We will read them as they happened.</p><p class="body-3 measure">A single prompt that says "build the sync", followed by an answer you did not question, is a weak submission.</p></div></div><div class="panel measure"><div class="panel-body"><h3 class="heading-4">3. Your git repository, with every commit</h3><p class="body-3 measure">Send the repository. Keep every commit and its message. Do not squash the work into one commit.</p><p class="body-3 measure">A message that says what you decided is useful. One commit called "final" is not useful.</p></div></div><div class="panel measure"><div class="panel-body"><h3 class="heading-4">4. Code, if you have time</h3><p class="body-3 measure">Code is optional. Node.js is welcome if you want to check a rule. It is not required, and we will not treat a missing program as a gap.</p><p class="body-3 measure">If you build it, use TypeScript on Node.js, version 20 or newer. It has to run with Node.js alone. Fake Salesforce. One command should run a demo from a fresh checkout. <code>npm install</code> plus that command is the upper bound.</p><p class="body-3 measure">The useful checks are the same four rules: a duplicate, an older event after a newer one, a webhook that must not be sent back to Salesforce, and a pending call that is still there after a restart while the fake Salesforce is down. The cap in the design is 100 requests per second. In a demo you may set a lower cap so the wait is visible. The code must enforce the cap it is given.</p><p class="body-3 measure">A service we would ship is out of scope.</p></div></div></div></div></section>

=== name the field / ordering ===
## 7. Rule: both sides change the same record

Decided. Full mechanism: [Architecture](https://github.com/hellosrijan/sync-data/wiki/Architecture), `apply(change)`.

- **Per field, the newest `occurred_at` wins.** On a webhook that's `occurredAt`. On a portal
  save it's our server clock when the save arrives (the portal sample has no time field), and
  the actor is the logged-in user (answers Q5).
- Each record stores the last-applied time and source of every field. A change is applied only
  if its `occurred_at` is newer than that field's stored time. Edits to different fields
  therefore both survive.
- **Every edit is written to the `field_change` history**, whether applied or superseded, inside
  the same transaction. It isn't a Django signal: signals miss superseded edits and bulk writes.
- Concurrent edits to one record are serialised with `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`.
- **Exact tie: Salesforce wins.**
- **Two portal users, same field (Q4):** both saves apply, and the later one is current. There's no conflict check, so the earlier editor isn't warned. Both edits stay in history.
- *Assumption:* Salesforce's clock and ours are NTP-synced, with drift well below the gap between
  real edits. *If not:* a later real edit can be ranked as earlier and recorded as superseded.

## 8. Rule: duplicate webhook, and an older webhook after a newer one

## Goals accomplished, and how AI was used

This project implements a two-way sync between Salesforce and an internal operations portal, built around one function, `apply()`, that enforces every rule the brief requires: deduplicating repeated webhooks via a unique event ID, resolving out-of-order changes by comparing each field's own timestamp rather than the whole record, breaking the sync loop by recognizing and suppressing our own echoed updates, and surviving a 6-hour Salesforce outage by queuing outbound changes durably in Postgres and draining them through a shared rate limiter once Salesforce recovers. AI (Claude Code) was used throughout, not as a single "build this" prompt but as an iterative collaborator: early sessions were spent designing the architecture, stress-testing choices like Django signals versus a single `apply()` gatekeeper, and resolving the brief's open questions one at a time with the reasoning written down; the actual build was then driven by a small team of specialized AI agents — a lead that owns requirements and verifies every acceptance criterion itself, a router that turns tasks into testable criteria, a coder, a tester, and a documentation agent — working through a phase-by-phase plan with task ledgers recording every hand-off; and once most phases were marked done, a separate round of independent AI-driven audits re-checked the actual code against the brief's own text rather than trusting our own notes, which is how several real bugs — including a rate limiter that could burst past the 100 req/s cap and a catch-up query that silently requested no field values — were caught before submission.

## 2. Systems, who calls whom, network boundary, interfaces

| Part | Runs where | Job | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Salesforce | Client's infrastructure | CRM. Sales users edit here. Has its own database. | Exists. Not ours. |
| Django web | Django 5.2 on the host (`runserver`) | HTTP entry point: the webhook endpoint (path A) and the portal API (path B entry, Customer, Contact, History, and SyncStatus views; built in phases 3 and 7). Serves `GET /api/v1/health/`, `POST /api/v1/webhooks/salesforce/`, Customer/Contact endpoints, and `GET /api/v1/sync/status/`. | Webhook endpoint built (phase 3, T-004); portal API built (phase 7). Portal login: DRF token per user (Q14, default); the Salesforce integration user comes from `manage.py create_integration_user`. |
| Dramatiq worker | Container `worker` | Runs Dramatiq actors and the dramatiq-crontab scheduler. | Runs dedupe retention actor `purge_expired_change_events` (daily at 02:00, `@cron` in `src/sync/tasks.py`), outbound worker `send_outbound` (with `max_retries=0`), recovery probe `probe_salesforce` (every 10 s, `@interval`), catch-up sync actors (`run_catchup`, `scheduled_catchup` every 5 min via `@interval`, built in phase 6), rate recovery `recover_limiter_rate` (every 30 s, `@interval`), backup sweep `sweep_outbound` (every 5 s, `@interval`), and dramatiq-crontab's heartbeat. |
| Postgres 17 | Container `db` | Portal copy of the records. | Running. Six models, migrations `0001_initial` and `0002_audit_columns` (§4). |
| Redis 7 | Container `redis` | Dramatiq broker (task messages), wake-up signal for the outbox, shared rate-limiter count, scheduler lock, health ping. | Running, AOF on. |

Stack in use: Python 3.14, Django 5.2, Django REST Framework, django-dramatiq, dramatiq-crontab,
Postgres 17, Redis 7 (see `pyproject.toml` and `docker-compose.yml`).

Who calls whom (from the brief):

1. Salesforce calls the Django web endpoint with a webhook (path A).
2. The Dramatiq worker calls the Salesforce record API with an outbound call (path B).
3. Sales users talk only to Salesforce. Portal users talk only to the portal.

Network boundary: HTTPS over the public internet is the only path between Salesforce and us. On
our side, the worker reaches `db` and `redis` by service name on the Compose network. The web
process runs on the host and reaches them on the published ports.

Two services (Q6, decided): the web process and the worker share only Postgres and Redis. Web →
worker: outbox rows in Postgres, plus a Redis nudge. Worker → web: nothing direct; results go to
Postgres. Either side can be down or redeployed without losing work.

Interface on each side:

| Path | Caller | Callee | Interface | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A. Webhook | Salesforce | Django web endpoint | HTTPS `POST` with DRF token authentication (Q11). `POST /api/v1/webhooks/salesforce/` (`openapi.yml`). | `eventId`, `recordId`, `objectType`, `occurredAt`, `changedBy`, `changedFields` (brief sample) |
| B. Outbound call | Dramatiq worker | Salesforce record API | HTTPS update via Salesforce's documented record API; creates as upsert by external ID (assumption Q13) | The fields the portal user changed, at their current values (§6). Creates also carry our record ID as the external ID. |
| B (ingress). Portal API | Portal user / frontend | Django web endpoint | HTTPS `GET`, `POST`, `PATCH` with DRF token authentication (Q14). Routes under `/api/v1/customer/` and `/api/v1/contact/` (`openapi.yml`). | CustomerWrite / ContactWrite schemas; responses include `syncState` (`synced`, `pending`, `needs_review`) |
| C. Catch-up | Dramatiq worker | Salesforce query API | HTTPS query for records changed since watermark minus overlap (`run_catchup`, assumption Q3) | SOQL query returning up to 2,000 records per page |
| Status | Staff operator | Django web endpoint | `GET /api/v1/sync/status/` (`IsAdminUser` staff auth) | JSON: Salesforce state, outbox counts, limiter rate, portal edits/s |
| Health | Operator | Django web | `GET /api/v1/health/` (public): 200 if Postgres and Redis both answer, else 503 | JSON: `postgres`, `redis` |

URL conventions (decided by the user): `config/urls.py` is the root URLconf and the only place that
defines `api/v1/` (it includes `utils.urls`, then `sync.urls`, plus `admin/`). Resource names are
singular (`api/v1/customer/`, `api/v1/customer/{id}/history/`). Every app has `urls.py` (with
`app_name`, never repeating the prefix) and `serializers.py`. The contract is [`openapi.yml`](openapi.yml).

Authentication: DRF `TokenAuthentication` only, `IsAuthenticated` by default, so a missing or bad token
gets 401. Health opts out with `AllowAny`. The Salesforce integration user is in the group
`salesforce-integration` (permission class `IsSalesforceIntegration`); create it and print its token with

Unreachable, timeout or 5xx: retry at 1, 2, 4, 8 s…, capped at 60 s. 429: pause the shared limiter until `Retry-After`, halve the rate, then add 5 req/s every 30 s back to 90. 400-type rejection: `needs_review`. 401/403: stop all sending and page. Its messages only wake the worker, and a timer task every 5 s backs up a lost wake-up. The pending call itself is an outbox row in Postgres. | If pending calls lived in Redis, `everysec` could lose about 1 s of them on a crash, and we would need `appendfsync always` or the outbox anyway. |

Transient failures are retried indefinitely (Q7). Dramatiq's dead-letter set is never used for outbound calls. | If dropping were acceptable, Dramatiq's default would do. All of them go through one shared limiter, so the total never exceeds 100. | Running at R = 100 leaves nothing for retries, so a burst of failures would push us over the cap. | Age of the oldest `pending` outbox row, while Salesforce is up | **> 2 min.** The 30 s sync target is clearly broken. Excludes outages, when rows are expected to wait. |

## Claude

Finished the pass. Good news first: the design doc is structurally very tight against the brief — I checked it point by point.

## Confirmed well-covered (no gap)
- `docs/design.md`'s 12 sections match the brief's exact outline, in order, headers 1–12.
- §1 assumptions sit at the top as required, and every one has an "if the other way" sentence.
- Customer/Contact field lists match the brief's field list exactly — no extra business fields.
- Webhook serializer field names (`eventId`, `recordId`, `objectType`, `occurredAt`, `changedBy`, `changedFields`) match the brief's sample exactly — nothing extra was added, so the "say why you added fields" clause doesn't even apply.
- "One service or two, and what crosses the boundary" (Q6) and "name the field used for ordering" (Q5: webhook → `occurredAt`; portal → server clock at save) are both explicitly answered.
- §11 has all three numbers with real alert thresholds ("page someone at"), §12's out-of-scope list matches the brief's exactly.
- `FakeSalesforce` satisfies "write your own fake CRM."

## New gaps from this top-down pass (distinct from the code bugs already in V-001/002/003)

1. **The 10-minute walkthrough doesn't exist yet** (`docs/walkthrough.md`, build-plan 9.2.1). It's tracked under Phase 9, which is the one phase still "In progress" — not missed, just still outstanding before this is submission-ready.

2. **A real conflict between the brief and a standing project decision, worth your call.** The brief's deliverable #2 is explicit: *"Include every chat you used for this task, every prompt, and every reply... A single prompt that says 'build the sync', followed by an answer you did not question, is a weak submission."* This repo's own `CLAUDE.md` says: *"Opencode chats are not exported (user decision)."* Given what we found earlier — a commit authored under a different identity, clearly from a parallel session doing real implementation work (phases 5–8) — if that work happened in opencode, excluding its chat history would leave the submission missing chats the brief explicitly asks for. Per `CLAUDE.md` itself, "If something here or in other docs disagrees with [the brief], the brief wins." Worth deciding explicitly: was that other session actually opencode, and if so, do you want it exported for submission purposes even though it isn't normally?

3. **Minor: commit granularity.** The brief says "do not squash the work into one commit." The most recent commit (`5e41728`) bundles two unrelated things — Phase 5 and the T-007 fix — into one. Not a real problem on its own, but phases 6–9 are entirely uncommitted right now; if they land as one or two giant commits instead of the same one-per-decision style the rest of the history uses, that would be a much bigger version of the same issue.

4. **The connective thread worth keeping in mind:** the brief states plainly, *"A rule that is only in the document, and a demo that does something else, will come up on the call."* That's exactly what V-001/V-002/V-003 already found — 5 critical and ~20 important places where the code diverges from `design.md`'s own stated rules (the echo bug, admin bypass, the rate-limiter burst, catch-up's broken query, portal-create atomicity, SyncStatus contract mismatches). None of that is new from this pass, but this read of the brief confirms those are precisely the kind of gap the evaluators say they'll probe — not cosmetic.

Nothing else looks missed. The one deliberate, large deviation (TypeScript/Node.js → Python/Django) is already honestly recorded in §12, so that one's handled — just worth keeping top of mind since it's the single biggest departure from the brief's literal ask.
